analysis.title: With Bond Vigilantes Away, Retail Will Play: NeoCloud Surge Erases Nasdaq's Post-Election Losses
key_insights: Nov 11 (Veterans Day, cash Treasuries closed, low liquidity): stocks ripped higher, led by tech/AI. Semis outperformed, hyperscalers lagged as a source of funds, Mag7 underperformed the SPX 493. NDX was up over 3% at its highs, and all major US indices are back in positive territory since the election.

Overnight AI catalysts: CoreWeave beat-and-raise, reports that Anthropic's bankers are weighing an IPO valuation of $1.5T or more, and word that OpenAI quarterly revenue hit $10B for the first time. Markets shrugged off Tuesday's hot CPI.

CRWV rose 25%. NeoClouds rose over 12% on the day and are up over 6% since the election. CoreWeave's results eased fears that financing limits would choke the AI buildout, and 'check receivers' outperformed 'check writers'.

Bull case on CoreWeave (Goldman): each customer contract is financed in a separate entity with 80%+ secured debt, repaid within the contract term, and CoreWeave keeps the GPUs. Capex levels off by 2028 and FCF turns positive in 2030. Tight supply supports $20-40M per MW and about $10B a year from re-renting paid-off GPUs.

Bear case on CoreWeave: management quotes $20-25M per MW but realized revenue is about $9-13M per MW. Both bears put next year's funding gap at about $33B. About 55 GW of new capacity is coming through 2028, roughly 20 times CoreWeave's share, threatening old-GPU rental prices while $47B of debt must be repaid before chips lose half their value.

The author sides with the bears on a three-year view and with the rally only while it lasts. All equity value sits in 'box six' of Goldman's funding diagram, the residual value of old GPUs after loans are repaid. Near-term test is the pricing of the investment-grade secured loan, expected at 7.0-7.5% within weeks. CRWV 2032s went out at 990bps over on Tuesday night.

Goldman flow: activity down about 20% vs the trailing two weeks, but market volumes +13% vs the 10dma and the floor tilted +13% better to buy, driven by HFs (+18%, large buy skews in Tech and Cons Disc). Long-only slightly better to buy, selling Tech and Cons Disc to buy HCare, Comms Svcs and Industrials.
Retail was very active: three stocks made up 32% of tape volume, and Goldman's Retail Favs basket (GSXURFAV) had its second-best day in 3 years.
Technicals: SPX back above its 100DMA, NDX back above its 200DMA, SOX near its 200DMA. Shorts were re-squeezed. Goldman's Broad AI basket rose 5% and is back above pre-election levels.

Mag7 dispersion: NVDA +4%, TSLA +3%, AMZN, GOOG and MSFT down about 2%. UBS: investors adding pick-and-shovel exposure while hyperscalers are a source of funds for the first time in a week. NVDA saw selling from active and retail investors ahead of next week's earnings, and is trying to recover part of the $430B of market cap lost this week.
The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index had its biggest gain since late July and retraced all of last week's selloff. UBS said semis were significantly better to buy, with HFs driving much of it.

Hedges were unwound: VIX fell to a 17 handle and pre-election lows. Investors sold existing long-vol exposure rather than adding, and VIX call selling may have contributed to the sharp decline in VVIX relative to VIX.

Rotation: UBS saw cyclicals outperforming defensives, selling in defensives and staples, demand for regional banks, and selective short covering in AI-related industrials. Consumer and bond-proxy sectors stay under pressure from the front-end repricing.
Energy led alongside a 2%+ rebound in crude on less constructive US-Iran diplomacy and renewed Strait of Hormuz concerns (Iran's IRGC claimed two tankers hit mines). Gains faded during the day.

Rates: after Tuesday's hawkish FedSpeak, Wednesday was quiet, but front-end rate-hike expectations rose. 2027 now fully prices 2x 25bps hikes, and 10Y note futures imply yields up 3-4bps, back above 5.00%. Treasury futures options saw upside-protection call spreads sold.

The dollar had its biggest 2-day jump since June and broke out of its 18-month range to its highest since May 2025. Gold fell back below $4,000. Bitcoin rallied back above $74,000 after testing 3-month lows the day before.

Bloomberg's Frank Monkam: the post-midterm reversal looks fragile. Aggregate implied and realized vol across equities, credit, rates and oil have not reset to prior lows, which raises contamination risk and keeps a higher floor under vol as inflation constraints limit policy backstops.
